medicines.whatItDoes: Helps your body use sugar better and lowers the sugar made by your liver.

howToTake.timing: Usually taken 1–2 times a day with meals.
howToTake.notes: Taking it with food can reduce stomach upset. Swallow with water.

medicines.keyPrecaution: Call your doctor if you have severe vomiting, deep/fast breathing, or unusual sleepiness (rare but serious).
medicines.missedDose: If you miss a dose, take it with food when you remember. If it is close to the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double up.
interactionsOrWarnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems.
Ask before drinking a lot of alcohol; it can raise side-effect risk.
Some imaging dyes (contrast) may require holding metformin.
redFlags: severe dehydration (not peeing much, very thirsty)

medicines.commonUse: High blood pressure (helps lower blood pressure)
medicines.whatItDoes: Relaxes blood vessels so blood can flow more easily.

howToTake.timing: Usually taken once daily, at the same time each day.
howToTake.notes: Can be taken with or without food.

medicines.keyPrecaution: Stand up slowly—this medicine can cause dizziness, especially when you first start it.
medicines.missedDose: Take it when you remember. If it is close to the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses at once.
interactionsOrWarnings: Tell your doctor if you have chest pain that is new or worse.
Ask about grapefruit products if your care team mentions it.

medicines.whatItDoes: Helps lower cholesterol and can reduce heart and stroke risk over time.

howToTake.timing: Once daily. Many people take it at bedtime, but follow your prescriber’s plan.
howToTake.notes: Can be taken with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day.

medicines.keyPrecaution: Call your doctor right away if you get unexplained muscle pain or weakness, especially with fever or dark urine.
medicines.missedDose: Take it when you remember the same day. If you remember the next day, skip the missed dose—do not double up.
interactionsOrWarnings: Avoid heavy alcohol use; it can stress the liver.
Some antibiotics/antifungals and grapefruit products can raise side effects—ask your pharmacist.

howToTake.timing: As needed, following the label or your doctor’s directions.
howToTake.notes: Can be taken with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, take with food.

medicines.keyPrecaution: Do not exceed 4,000 mg (4 g) per day from ALL sources. Many cold/flu products also contain acetaminophen.
commonSideEffects: usually well tolerated when used correctly
medicines.missedDose: If you take it on a schedule and miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is close to the next dose. Do not double up.
interactionsOrWarnings: Avoid alcohol if possible; mixing can harm the liver.
Ask your doctor if you have liver disease.

medicines.whatItDoes: Lowers the acid made in your stomach, which can help heartburn and protect the stomach and esophagus.

howToTake.timing: Usually once daily, about 30 minutes before breakfast.
howToTake.notes: Best before a meal so it can work well. Swallow whole with water.

medicines.keyPrecaution: Tell your doctor if you get ongoing diarrhea, because it can rarely be a sign of an infection.
medicines.missedDose: Take it when you remember that day. If it is close to the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double up.
interactionsOrWarnings: Long-term daily use should be reviewed with your doctor.
Tell your doctor about any blood thinners or HIV medicines you take.
